title: Prophet Musa (AS)
intro: Saved as a baby on the Nile, raised in Pharaoh’s palace, chosen at the burning fire – Musa (AS) led his people to freedom.

learn.html: After Yusuf (AS) passed away to the better, everlasting world, life for the Children of Isra’il (Bani Isra’il) became harder and harder, until in time they were enslaved by Pharaoh and his people.

It is told that one night Pharaoh dreamed of a fire coming from Jerusalem into Egypt and burning it, but sparing the Children of Isra’il. In the morning he called his dream-readers. They told him that a boy would be born among the Children of Isra’il who would end his rule. Pharaoh at once ordered that every newborn boy be killed.

At that time one of Allah’s chosen messengers was born – Musa (AS). His mother went to the banks of the Nile, far from other people’s eyes, to give birth. She felt joy and fear at the same time: joy because of her son, and fear because of Pharaoh’s order.

Allah (SWT) inspired her to put her son in a basket woven from reeds and let it float down the Nile. Her daughter followed the basket along the river bank. By Allah’s decree the basket reached Pharaoh’s palace. Pharaoh’s wife Asiya had it brought to her. Seeing the baby, she felt great love for him and asked her husband to accept him and not fear him, because they would raise him in their palace.
When it was time to feed the baby, he would not accept any nursing mother – until his own mother was brought.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: So We returned him to his mother, so that she would be happy and not grieve, and know that Allah’s promise is true – but most of them do not know. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Qasas 28:13, meaning)</small>

Musa (AS) grew up in Pharaoh’s palace as a member of the family, surrounded by a beautiful and comfortable life. He thought of Pharaoh’s family as his own, and knew his real mother as his nurse. Asiya loved him with all her heart as her own child. He grew into a young man of great strength, skill, knowledge and wisdom – gifts from Allah: When he reached his full strength and maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge – that is how We reward those who do good. (Al-Qasas 28:14, meaning)

After an unfortunate incident with a man from Pharaoh’s people, Musa (AS), by Allah’s permission, left Egypt and went to Madyan. At the wells of Madyan he saw many shepherds watering their flocks, and two girls standing apart, holding their animals back from the water. “Why are you doing this?” Musa asked. “We don’t water our flock until the shepherds leave, and our father is very old, so there is no one to look after and protect us.”

Musa (AS) watered their flock and sat in the shade of a tree to rest. Tired and hungry, he made dua to Allah for the food he needed. Soon one of the girls came and said her father wanted to reward him for what he had done. Their father was Shu‘ayb. Musa married the younger sister and worked on Shu‘ayb’s land, and after ten years he took his family back across Mount Sinai.
Crossing the mountain, he saw a fire in the distance and went towards it to bring his family a torch. At that moment he received the first revelation from Allah and became Allah’s messenger.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Has the story of Musa reached you? When he saw a fire and said to his family: “Stay here – I see a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, or find guidance by the fire.” When he came to it, he was called: “O Musa! I am your Lord, so take off your shoes – you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.” <small>(Qur’an, Ta-Ha 20:9–13, meaning)</small>

Allah sent him to Pharaoh with clear proofs: a staff that turned into a snake, and a hand that became shining white. These miracles confirmed he was sent by Allah. Musa also asked Allah to give him his brother Harun as a helper, and his dua was answered. Pharaoh had become arrogant and said to his chiefs: “I am your lord, the most high!” (An-Nazi‘at 79:24, meaning)

When Musa showed him the proofs of prophethood and called him to believe in the One God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Pharaoh rejected the truth. He gathered his people at an agreed place, with the best magicians at their head, who helped him rule and keep people in disbelief.

learn.title: 📖 The magicians
learn.html: They said: “O Musa, will you throw, or shall we throw first?” “You throw,” he said – and suddenly their ropes and sticks seemed to him to be moving because of their magic, and Musa felt fear inside. We said: “Don’t be afraid – you will win! Throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they made. What they made is only a magician’s trick, and a magician never succeeds, wherever he comes.” <small>(Qur’an, Ta-Ha 20:65–69, meaning)</small>
When the magicians saw that Musa’s miracle was real, they believed and fell into sajdah to the Lord of the worlds – despite Pharaoh’s threats and punishment.

By Allah’s command, Musa (AS) led his people out of slavery at night, with Pharaoh and his army close behind. The sea stood in front of them. Allah commanded Musa to strike the sea with his staff; he did, and by Allah’s decree the sea split apart. Musa and the believers crossed, and Pharaoh and his army drowned when the sea returned to how it was.

learn.title: 📖 Too late
learn.html: When the waves closed over him, Pharaoh said: “I believe there is no god except the One the Children of Isra’il believe in, and I submit!” – “Now? When before you disobeyed and spread corruption? Today We will save only your body, so that you are a sign for those after you.” <small>(Qur’an, Yunus 10:90–92, meaning)</small>
So Musa (AS) and his people were saved, and Pharaoh’s body was preserved as a lesson for those who are arrogant towards Allah and make others equal to Him.

practice.title: The story of Musa (AS)
items: Pharaoh orders every newborn boy to be killed
Musa’s mother puts him in a basket on the Nile
Asiya takes him into Pharaoh’s palace
Musa helps two girls water their flock in Madyan
Allah speaks to Musa at the fire in the valley of Tuwa
Musa’s staff swallows the magicians’ tricks
The sea parts and the believers are saved

practice.title: People in the story
pairs: Said: “I am your lord, the most high”
Fed him when he refused all others

questions.q: Why was it a dangerous time for a baby boy?
options: Pharaoh ordered every newborn boy to be killed
There was a war in Makkah

questions.q: How did Allah bring Musa back to his mother?
options: He refused every nurse until his mother came

questions.q: What were Musa’s two signs before Pharaoh?
options: The staff that became a snake, and the shining white hand

questions.q: What did the magicians do when they saw the truth?
options: They believed and fell into sajdah

questions.q: How were Musa (AS) and his people saved?
options: Allah parted the sea when Musa struck it with his staff

questions.q: Why did Allah preserve Pharaoh’s body?
options: As a sign and lesson for those after him

practice.title: Questions and task
prompts: ❓ Where and in what times was Musa (AS) born? What did his mother do with him?
❓ Where did Musa grow up, and how did Allah bring him and his mother back together?
❓ How were Musa (AS) and his people saved?

🔎 Task: The Qur’an says Pharaoh’s body will be preserved as a warning to all people until the Day of Judgement. Find out what researchers say about where Pharaoh’s body was found and where it is today.
